newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Closing positions in Alpha-Beta.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Closing positions in Alpha-Beta.

text.p: Investors were closing positions in Alpha-Beta Technology Inc options as the stock fell sharply on news of disappointing Phase III trials for an experimental drug, traders said Monday.
In late action, Alpha-Beta was down 4-9/16 at 6-1/4 on more than 7.6 million shares. The stock was just a quarter point off its session low.
Among the options, the August 7-1/2 put was most active, with turnover of roughly 13,130 contracts. The August 10 call traded about 10,500.
"There's obviously disappointment," said Michael Young, a market maker in Alpha-Beta options at the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE).
"My assumption is most of the option volume is closing positions," he said. "Open interest should drop significantly."
Young said implied volatility in the options, which had held steady at high levels for a couple of weeks, had come down significantly after the news came out.
Even so, some volatilities remained over 100 percent.
Early Monday, the company said its anti-infection drug failed to show any statistical significance in pivotal trials involving 1,177 patients.

The company's chief executive told Reuters he still hoped to seek U.S. Food and Drug Administration permission by late 1997 to market the drug, Betafectin, to one group of patients he said clearly benefitted from the drug.
Other busy Alpha-Beta options included the August 10, with volume of 4,055 contracts and the August 7-1/2 and 12-1/2 calls, which traded 2,165 and 2,285 contracts, respectively.
In other trading, investors were closing out positions in options on a couple Latin American American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), namely YPF SA and Telebras .
The YPF August 30 call traded about 3,360 contracts by afternoon.
"A customer bought them a couple weeks ago and it looks like he's just closing them out," said Brian Korbell at LETCO in Chicago. "He's been selling them."
The option was trading down 1/2 at 1-11/16 in late activity. Its open interest was 20,331.
Korbell added that some investors were closing positions in Telebras.
"Customers have been selling a little September premium," he said, explaining they were mainly selling the September 150 calls, which traded a total of 6,190 contracts.
"They've been buying the August 145s and selling some August 140s," he added. The August 145 calls traded about 2,450 contracts and the August 140 calls traded 5,625.
The August 140 puts traded about 1,100 and the August 145 puts traded fewer than 200 contracts.
"Most of it is institutional," Korbell said of the action.
